full_judgment: 2. Facts leading to this, in short are that the petitioner Mr. A.Y. Masihuzzaman, a Senior Advocate of this Court, filed a petition of complaint before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka under section 499 and 500 of the Penal Code stating that the petitioner, an Advocate 01" the Supreme Court of Bangladesh having reputation as an honest and hardworking lawyer and had appeared in a number or cases both in the High Court and in the Court before the District Judge. The petitioner's mother along with his brothers and sisters are owners in joint possession of 33 acres of land in R.S. Plot No. 341 of C.S. Khatian No. 315 and R.S. Khatian No.322 of Mouza Barabo, Shymali within Mohamrnadpur P.S. The petitioner's mother had appointed care taker Abdul Kalam to look after that property. He had been residing therein in, a Collage constructed by the mother of the petitioner. 1'1I1r. Shah Alarn who is the opposite party in this petition and who is a local Municipal Commissioner is an influenced man in the locality. He in collusion with the Settlement Officer recorded the said property in the name or one Abdus Sauar, behind the back of the real owner or the property and since then Mr. Shah Alam (opposite Party No.1) with the help of other opposite parties had been threatening to dispossess-his mother and his mother's brothers and sister-from-the-said property by evicting the care taker. In that view of the matter, the petitioner's mother, her brothers and sisters, who are all respectable educated persons, on their own accord filed a suit, being Title Suit No. 82 of 1978 in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for a declaration or title in the suit property. In that title Suit No. 82 of 1978 the present petitioner Mr. A.Y. Masihuzzaman is the filing Advocate. When that was the matter Mr. Shah Alam, opposite party No.1 trespassed in to the property with the help of the opposite parties and hired persons and attempted to evict the said care taker Abul Kalam and demolished the collage on 15.2.78 but Shah A lam failed to take forcible possession due to the resistance of the said care taker and his brother. Failing to take possession Shah Alam and his brother kid- napped the said care taker and handed them over to the Police. A petition of complaint being G.D. Entry No. 7(;6 dated 15.2.1978 was lodged before the police at Mohammadpur Station as a result of which the care taker AbulKalam and his brother were re- leased. On the basis of the said incident, a complaint case was filed before the S.D.O. Sadar, Dhaka being petition Case No. 367/ AI of 1978 under sections 148/448/365/342/336/323 of the Penal Code and cognizance taken under sections 342/448 by the Court and on being summoned the opposite parties 1-5 and 8 were released on bail. In the meantime, an order of ad-interim injunction was also obtained in the Title Suit No. 82 of 1978 restraining the defendants-opposite party No.1 and others from entering into the property at Shayamali and from disturbing or interfering in any way with the peaceful possession and enjoyment of the property by the plaintiffs in that suit. The opposite parties however continue to threat the said care taker Abul Kalam in order to frighten him to leave the property. Having caused a serious apprehension of breach of peace the said caretaker took shelter of law by filing a petition before the S.D.O. (South) Dhaka under sections 107 and 117 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, being case No.757 of 1978. The said proceeding under section 107 has been drawn up against the opposite parties in the said case on 23.10.79. A show cause notice was issued on which the opposite parties appeared and resisted the case by filing a jointly written statement. The opposite parties in the said written statement 'stated in 'paragraph 8(i) thus. "That this opposite party No.1 now strongly believes that Abul Kalam having fallen in precarious position took shelter of the said Advocate Mr. Masihuzzaman who has been trying to harass the opposite party No.1 by filing cases after cases" and stated further in paragraph 8(j) thus:- "that Advocate Mr. Masihuzzaman has been failing cases after cases against opposite party No.1 and his men only to harass the opposite party No.1. The petitioner Abul Kalam is not the caretaker of Begum Badiuzzaman or anybody of her family. That the said Advocate had crocodile eyes on the said land and as such these are his creation only to harass the opposite party No.21 and in paragraph 8(k) it has been stated thus :- that the petitioner has been induced by the Advocate to file this case against the opposite parties with some false fabricated allegations and there is no apprehension of breach of peace."
